title: dev-onboard-how / dev-onboard-why card: one area, one lens, every claim cited
description: Written by one dev-onboard-how or dev-onboard-why agent to <evid_root>/onboard/<project>/cards/<area>.<lens>.json. A card is one reader's account of one area through one lens: how (what the code is and does, cited to file and line) or why (the reasons, cited to the record or marked as inference). check_card.py checks it against the repo before dev-onboard-map reads it, so a claim that cites nothing real never reaches the map. Claims share the map's claim shape. See docs/onboarding-loop.md.

commit.description: The commit the reader looked at; the survey's commit.

area.description: The survey area id this card covers.

mode.description: fresh = first read. missing = the map had nothing on the focus topics. correct = claims named in focus were graded wrong and are re-checked from the code. deepen = answers were vague; narrow the cites and walk the flow. The router picks the mode from the quiz's failure class.

focus.description: For a relearn: the question topics or claim ids this card was asked about. Empty on a fresh read.

summary.description: Two or three sentences on this area through this lens, the way a senior engineer would say it out loud.

claims.description: Atomic, cited claims, same shape as map claims.

id.description: <area>.h<n> on a how card, <area>.w<n> on a why card. dev-onboard-map keeps the id, so a question that cites it stays valid across rounds.

kind.description: what = what a thing is. how = a runtime flow or mechanism. where = where something lives. owner = which module owns a piece of state or a decision. why = the reason it is built this way. rule = where new code of a given kind belongs (the architect lens). gotcha = a trap a newcomer would hit. command = how to build, test, run or lint.

text.description: The claim in one or two plain sentences. No hedging words; confidence carries the hedge.

cites.description: What the claim rests on. Code cites carry path and lines; record cites carry ref. Empty only for a why claim marked source=inference.

symbol.description: A name that must appear in the cited lines. The grader checks it, which catches a cite that drifted.

ref.description: A record pointer for a why claim: commit:<sha>, pr:<number>, doc:<path>.

evidence.description: How far the claim was proven. said = asserted only (never enough for a non-why claim). pointed = a real file and line. walked = the flow was traced step by step and the bad case does not reach. ran = a command or test that calls the real code showed it.

confidence.description: Mainly for why claims. certain = the record says so in the authors' words. likely = a strong inference. guessing = filling a gap. A why claim that is an inference may not be certain.

drops.description: Correct mode: map claims this reader checked and found wrong, with what the code actually says. dev-onboard-map removes them instead of patching them.

replaced_by.description: The new claim id that says it correctly, when there is one.

gaps.description: What this reader could not answer from its sources, in plain words. On a why card these are questions the record does not answer; they go to the map's open questions, never get filled with a guess.

read.description: Files or record refs the reader opened, for the decision log.
